title: Fournier's theorem: graphs whose maximum-degree vertices induce a forest are of class one
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of Fournier's theorem (1973): if the vertices of maximum degree of a finite simple graph G induce a forest, then G has a proper edge colouring with Δ(G) colours (fournier: G.lineGraph.Colorable G.maxDegree under (G.induce {v | G.degree v = G.maxDegree}).IsAcyclic). The proof takes an edge-minimal subgraph H of G that is not Δ(G)-edge-colourable; Vizing's theorem gives Δ(H) = Δ(G), and Vizing's adjacency lemma applied to every edge xy of H gives a neighbour of x of maximum degree other than y, so the maximum-degree vertices of H span a subgraph of minimum degree at least 2 inside the forest, which is impossible (the end of a longest path). Vizing's theorem and the adjacency lemma are imported as lake dependencies from PALOMAR-2026-10-15-000004 and PALOMAR-2026-11-04-000009. One statement; no definitions beyond Mathlib's.
